anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 mine is a 5x5x3 isometric pile with four diamonds, one visible screen, one lava hazard, one support hazard, no sealed-target prerequisite, and a click-ray/durability extraction sequence. Even Unwatched Wing L1 instead requires first-person corridor navigation, three ordered observer-release transitions, and a final darkness transfer. The mine has richer occlusion, material hazards, and view rotation; Unwatched Wing has more dependent temporal/navigation state, so its L1 is above this L1 reference on sequence and exploration but below it on voxel-specific precision and hazard recovery.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 constellation is one 680x410 active-vision field: 112 coherent stars plus noise and two decoy basins, with a single final click accepted within 28 pixels. Its surfaces change how the cursor is positioned, but there is no multi-stage world state after selection. Unwatched Wing L1 already adds a first-person map, ordered target progression, observer equipment, and exact dark docking, so it is more demanding in dependent state and navigation even though the constellation has a denser 2D search signal.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 board has three ordered lamps, three walls, and three wells under deterministic 50 ms ball physics, with continuous analog tilt in Full and compass choices in Simplified. The grader's minimum tick and control-change requirements are verifier witnesses, not difficulty credit; the physical momentum, collisions, ordered lamps, and hazard resets are the active burden. Unwatched Wing L3 has less continuous motor control but more first-person line-of-sight and observer-equipment state. This places Unwatched Wing L3 near the L3/L4 boundary and supports, rather than undercuts, its L4 baseline.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 courier is an 18x11 warehouse with five barrier gates, four sparse scanners, and a hidden die orientation that must be updated across a long valid roll sequence; the grader independently applies orientation algebra and gate checks. Unwatched Wing L4 has six ordered target plinths, two probe-held blind handoffs, two target-linked lights, first-person collision/line-of-sight navigation, and exact final darkness. Both have several dependent stages and memory of a changing hidden or equipment state. Blind Dice has deeper orientation planning and a longer roll path, while Unwatched Wing has stronger visual exploration and equipment-state burden; the current L4 assignment is a reasonable cross-mechanic match.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 candy task requires four valid swaps on a changing 5x5 board, exact score, at least seven cascade waves, a short refill preview, and avoiding terminal black licorice. Each accepted swap changes the later decision problem and the grader replays the changing board, refill cursor, score, and waves. Unwatched Wing L5 adds seven ordered target positions, three probe-held thresholds, three light interlocks, a longer labyrinth, decoys, and narrower observation ranges, but its protocol is more structured and less combinatorial than Exact-Change's exact-score choices. It is a credible upper profile, but the source alone does not prove it exceeds the approved L4/L5 planning boundary.

visible_baseline_solution: From screenshots, read the named exhibit in the dossier and use the first-person viewport and reticle to navigate the visible museum corridor. The current unstable exhibit is rendered at the current target plinth; ordinary target plinths, nearby isolator lights, labels at close range, and split-arrow markers are visible when line of sight and lighting permit. Keep the current target observed long enough to establish it, then release observation by turning or moving beyond line of sight/range with the lamp and any target-linked light disabled. At an arrow-marked handoff, aim the probe at the old plinth, open the viewer, turn the lamp off, and walk beyond the turn while the live probe keeps the old plinth observed; after the release threshold is reached, close the viewer and recall the probe before continuing. Disable each nearby target-linked light before releasing its target. At the last target, stand within the pedestal radius and make the viewport, probe, lamp, viewer, and every visible light dark; the canvas must become black and the dock transition then occurs. Full uses WASD, viewport drag, viewport probe clicks, and F/V/R/E; Simplified uses the labelled movement, turn, lamp, viewer, probe, recall, and isolator buttons. No private route or page-state data is part of this solution.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current baseline is not merely a six-step repetition. It combines first-person spatial exploration and line-of-sight control with a changing target cursor, two probe-held handoff states, two target-linked light states, decoy identity tracking, and a terminal all-observers-off condition. The grader replays these dependencies rather than trusting a completion flag. It is materially above the approved L1 voxel extraction and L2 constellation tasks, comparable in dependent-state depth to the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier, and less combinatorially choice-heavy than the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade. L4 is therefore a defensible provisional absolute level and the source supports keeping it.

Success requires replayed dock occupancy, all required pin steps, no active observers, and measured darkness thresholds.

uncertainties: This is a source-calibrated level judgment, not human or computer-use-agent calibration.
Seed-dependent route transforms, target placements, decoy placements, and palettes can change visual navigation burden within a profile.
The source shows the browser contract for honest rendering; page-state inspection would be outside the screenshot-only task boundary and was not treated as a normal solution.
Visual legibility, probe-feed interpretation, and whether the generic instruction is sufficient for first-time users need parent runtime and human checks.

concise_summary: Keep The Unwatched Wing at its current L4/full baseline and retain the five ordered profiles. Source supports genuine increases from observer-release state, probe-held handoffs, light interlocks, route exploration, and tighter visibility controls; the absolute L5 comparison remains provisional because its protocol is more structured than the approved changing-board L5 anchor.
limitations: No browser, runtime, multi-seed, human, or computer-use-agent check was run.
Absolute difficulty estimates and seed-to-seed visual burden remain uncalibrated.
Historical pre-controls preservation cannot be established from the assigned source snapshot.
The report evaluates the normal screenshot-only UI path; hidden page-state or source inspection is explicitly outside that path.
